opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
“Therefore, whoever breaks one of the least of these commandments and teaches others to do so will be called least in the Kingdom of heaven. But whoever obeys and teaches these commandments will be called greatest in the Kingdom of heaven.”
These words come from the Sermon on the Mount in the Gospel of Matthew (Matthew 5:19). Jesus has just said something very important: he did not come to abolish the law, but to fulfill it.
At that moment, many people listening might have wondered if his teaching meant the commandments no longer mattered. Jesus answers that concern directly.
He says that whoever loosens even the smallest commandment and encourages others to do the same will be called least in the Kingdom of heaven. But the person who lives the commandments and teaches them faithfully will be called great.
The point is not legalism. Jesus is not talking about mechanically following rules. He is pointing to something deeper: integrity between belief, action, and influence.
Our lives teach constantly.
 What we tolerate, excuse, or dismiss teaches others what is acceptable.
 What we live faithfully encourages others to live faithfully as well.
So Jesus raises the standard. The law is not merely about external compliance. It is about the formation of the heart and the example we set for others.
In the Kingdom of heaven, greatness is not measured by power, status, or recognition. It is measured by faithfulness—quietly living the truth and helping others walk in it.
That is the challenge embedded in this short passage:
 Live the commandments sincerely, and teach them not only with words, but with the witness of your life
